chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Later days at the Grand Terrace and why Hines broke up the band
summary: Business slumped but Hines left over a plan for a cocktail lounge.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: What were some of the interesting things that happened at the Grand Terrace in the early days,
Well, I can't remember too much. Too many things happening.
Were the crowds varied? You said earlier that the pay depended on how the business was. So the crowds were up and down, would depend on what you --
Yeah, well that got along toward the last.
Uh-huh. What did the union say about that?
Wasn't nothing they could do. The union had to go along with them, too.
Is that why Earl finally left the Grand Terrace?

No. He broke up his band. While we was at the Terrace. He didn't leave on account of the money, he just left on account of he was intending to get like a cocktail lounge and play in it himself. That was his first idea of breaking up the band, and then after --

In Chicago. Then after he got into the thing and it looked like it wasn't going to turn out so well, he decided to go back to the band. And he reorganized the band. But it wasn't the money -- wasn't the reason why he left the Grand Terrace.
